sub_answers.sub_question: What documented financial difficulties, sponsorship withdrawals, or insolvency events has the club experienced and when?
sub_answers.text: CFR Cluj entered insolvency amid financial difficulties after the 2014–15 season which led to large performance problems and point deductions in that period [d2376249s5p0]. Players at CFR were not fully remunerated, prompting the Romanian Football Federation to deduct 24 points (later restored) during the insolvency episode [d2376249s5p0]. Kagua-Erave FC had reports in early May 2019 that players had not been paid, threatening the club's participation in the 2019 NSL playoffs before they eventually fielded a side [d60559687s1p0].

sub_answers.text: CFR Cluj's owner Pászkány faced legal charges and was reported as having neglected the team during the financially troubled period after 2012 [d2376249s5p0]. The Romanian Football Federation sanctioned CFR with a 24-point deduction over unpaid players, a punitive action that affected the club's standing [d2376249s5p0]. Kagua-Erave FC's players went unpaid in May 2019, which created public doubt about the club's ability to participate in the playoffs [d60559687s1p0].

sub_answers.text: Papua New Guinea first gained One-Day International status by finishing fourth in the 2014 World Cup Qualifier, which determined their eligibility for ODI matches [d3106308s0p0]. Papua New Guinea lost both their ODI and T20I status in March 2018 after losing a playoff match against Nepal during the 2018 Cricket World Cup Qualifier, a competitive-result-based mechanism that directly removed their international status [d3106308s0p0]. The ICC decided in April 2018 to grant full T20I status to all its Members, meaning all T20 matches between Papua New Guinea and other ICC members from 1 January 2019 onward carried full T20I status regardless of previous qualification pathways [d3106308s0p0]. Papua New Guinea reclaimed ODI status on 26 April 2019 by defeating Oman to secure a top-four finish in the 2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two, where finishing positions determined promotion to ODI status [d3106308s0p0]. Papua New Guinea again lost ODI status in 2023 after a 117-run defeat against the USA, showing that single-match outcomes in qualification events directly affected their tiered status [d3106308s0p0].
